1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

12 Technical Improvements that reduce consumption
12.1 Start-Stop function
This system reduces fuel consumption and the emission of greenhouse gases.
The system is activated automatically when starting the vehicle. When driving, the system stops the engine (stand-by) if the vehicle comes to a halt (traffic jams, traffic lights, etc.).
The vehicle starts when the brake pedal is released in automatic vehicles or the clutch is activated in vehicles with manual gear change.
(Página 278 del manual 'Learning to drive')

VISIBILITY
 
7 Transparent elements around the cockpit
The glass and mirrors enables the driver to obtain and retain the maximum vision possible:
They must not:
- Cause the images seen to be deformed or altered. Or
- Cause colours to be distorted. (For example this could cause confusion by changing colours on road signs etc.)
Note: It is prohibited to use nonaccredited tinted or coloured glass.
(Página 88 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Maneouvres    
   
3 Joining the traffic flow
3.3 Obligation to assist this manoeuvre
Although drivers that wish to join into the flow of traffic, must give way to other motorists, if at all possible, other drivers have the obligation to help to facilitate the manouevre .i.e. assist others to join the traffic flow.
Motorists are obliged to help public transport vehicles that have stopped at an official stop, and need to remerge into the traffic flow.
(Página 185 del manual 'Learning to drive')
